deliverables: Two advisory councils chartered with COI policies, named members, first meetings, and on-chain charters within 6 weeks.
A dOSPO 501(c)(3) public charity legal entity with governance documents and operator agreement by week 24, subject to U.S. legal processes and governance.
Quarterly public outcome reports published on-chain with Mill Law Firm financial review attached.
A dependency audit with SBOMs, centrality scores, bus factor assessments, coverage gap analysis, and published retainer rubric by week 12.
A first Maintenance Fund retainer cohort with published rubric scores, signed agreements, on-chain disbursements, and advisory feedback by week 18.
A public CHAOSS-aligned health dashboard for funded projects by week 16.
End-of-term portfolio review with rationale and Mill Law Firm financial audit within 14 days of term end.
request.recipient: Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting as administrator at withdrawal, with a planned dOSPO 501(c)(3) legal entity transition target subject to governance.
request.what: Establish a one-year independent Cardano decentralized Open Source Program Office and Open Maintenance Framework program to manage open source sustainability funding and related governance, legal, reporting, and advisory infrastructure.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 4,094,000 ADA over 12 months to fund the revised Cardano dOSPO and OMF program.
Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting is designated as the sole Article II.7.5 administrator from the moment of treasury withdrawal through the 12-month period.
Mill Law Firm is designated as independent financial auditor on a quarterly cadence through month 12.
Final allocation authority remains with the administrator, while advisory councils publish written feedback before each disbursement.
The proposal states that DReps can replace the administrator or shut down the initiative through an on-chain Info Action and return remaining funds if governance is unsatisfied.
The Maintenance Fund would deploy 2,000,000 ADA over 12 months to support high-risk Cardano open source infrastructure using dependency centrality and bus factor data.
The proposer claims that existing Cardano open source infrastructure relies on fragmented coordination, volunteer effort, short-term grants, or individual organizations.
The proposer claims a personal track record from founding Open Source Cowboy Consulting and previously building Cardano open source governance and OSPO functions at Intersect.
The proposal claims 90 pages of expert-vetted whitepapers and YouTube explanatory material detail how the structure will operate.

The proposal sets KPIs including funding 15 or more high-centrality projects by month 12, funding 40% of top-50 dependencies, publishing all four quarterly reports, and targeting bus factor 2+ for all top-20 centrality projects.

summary: The document proposes a 12-month, 4,094,000 ADA program administered initially by Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting to create and operate dOSPO/OMF open source sustainability programs, with advisory councils, quarterly audits, public reporting, dependency-based project selection, and governance replaceability mechanisms.
